sections.title: Section 1: East India Company's Trade Monopoly Extension & Governance Powers

masteryZone.q: Question 1 (Section 1): True or False: The Charter Act of 1793 extended the overriding powers originally given to Lord Cornwallis to all future Governors-General.
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 1: The Act generalized the override power to all future Governors-General and Governors of Bombay/Madras.

masteryZone.q: Question 2 (Section 1): The Charter Act of 1793 extended the trade monopoly of the East India Company for a period of ________ years.
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 2: The trade monopoly was extended for another 20 years.

masteryZone.q: Question 3 (Section 1): Match the provisions of the Charter Act of 1793 with their descriptions:

options.text: A. Extended for 20 years
B. Extended to all future Governors-General
C. Supersedes local Governors when present
D. Excluded from Council unless specially appointed

masteryZone.sol: Explanation 3: All matches represent the core administrative clauses of the Act of 1793.

masteryZone.q: Question 4 (Section 1): Which subsequent Act eventually ended the Company's trade monopoly in India (except tea & China trade) extended by the 1793 Act?
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 4: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the trade monopoly in India, except for tea and trade with China.

masteryZone.q:
Question 5 (Section 1): Assertion (A): The Governor-General of Bengal was given more powers and control over Madras and Bombay Presidencies under the 1793 Act.
Reason (R): The Act of 1793 extended the override power to all future Governors-General and subordinated provincial Governors.
opts: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 5: Both statements are true, and the reason explains the subordination of provincial authorities under the Governor-General.

masteryZone.q:
Question 6 (Section 1): Consider the following statements regarding the Governor-General's powers under the Charter Act of 1793:
1. The Governor-General could override his Council only in matters of peace, safety, or interests of the empire.
2. When visiting Madras or Bombay, the Governor-General was subordinate to the local Governor.
Which of the statement(s) is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 6: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Governor-General superseded the local Governor when present in those Presidencies.

masteryZone.q: Question 7 (Section 1): Which of the following governance powers were extended or established by the Charter Act of 1793? (Select all that apply)
opts: Overriding veto power for all future Governors-General
More control of the Governor-General over Bombay and Madras
Establishment of the Board of Control
Appointment of separate Governors for Bombay and Madras
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 7: Veto power and control over subordinate presidencies were features of the 1793 Act. The Board of Control was established in 1784, and separate Governors already existed.

masteryZone.q: Question 8 (Section 1): What did the Charter Act of 1793 do to the trade monopoly of the East India Company?
opts: Extended it for 20 years
Abolished it completely
Extended it indefinitely
Abolished it for all goods except salt
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 8: The Act extended the Company's trade monopoly in India for 20 years.

sections.title: Section 2: Financial Arrangements, Board of Control Payments & Judicial Restructuring

masteryZone.q: Question 1 (Section 2): True or False: The Charter Act of 1793 abolished the Maal Adalats (revenue courts), transferring their jurisdiction to the Diwani Adalats.
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 1: The Act consolidated the separation of revenue and judiciary, abolishing Maal Adalats.

masteryZone.q: Question 2 (Section 2): The Charter Act of 1793 required the East India Company to pay £________ annually to the British Government from its surplus revenue.
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 2: The Company was required to pay a fixed sum of 500,000 pounds annually.

masteryZone.q: Question 3 (Section 2): Match the financial and judicial aspects of the 1793 Act with their descriptions:

items.left: II. Annual Payment to British Crown

options.text: A. Charged to Indian revenues
B. Fixed at £500,000 annually
C. Abolished by separating revenue from judiciary
D. Vested with jurisdiction over revenue disputes

masteryZone.sol: Explanation 3: All matches represent the financial and judicial clauses of the Act of 1793.

masteryZone.q: Question 4 (Section 2): Which specific courts were abolished under the Charter Act of 1793 due to the separation of revenue from the judiciary?
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 4: Maal Adalats (revenue courts) were abolished by the Act.

masteryZone.q:
Question 5 (Section 2): Assertion (A): The payment of Board of Control salaries from Indian revenues was criticized by Indian nationalists.
Reason (R): This provision represented a systematic 'Drain of Wealth' from India to Great Britain without any return services.
opts: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are false
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 5: Both statements are true, and the reason correctly explains the nationalist criticism of wealth drainage.

masteryZone.q:
Question 6 (Section 2): Consider the following statements regarding the financial provisions of the Charter Act of 1793:
1. The Board of Control salaries were charged to the British Treasury until 1858.
2. The Company was mandated to pay £500,000 annually to the British Government.
Which of the statement(s) is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 6: Statement 1 is incorrect because the salaries were charged to Indian revenues in 1793. Statement 2 is correct.

masteryZone.q: Question 7 (Section 2): Which of the following judicial or financial provisions were enacted by the Charter Act of 1793? (Select all that apply)
opts: Abolition of Maal Adalats
Salaries of Board of Control paid out of Indian revenues
Introduction of permanent settlement of land revenue
Establishment of high courts in Bombay and Madras
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 7: The Act of 1793 abolished Maal Adalats and shifted Board salaries. The permanent settlement was introduced by Lord Cornwallis as a separate administrative code in 1793, and High Courts were established in 1861.

masteryZone.q: Question 8 (Section 2): Under the Charter Act of 1793, the salaries of the Board of Control members and staff were charged to:
opts: Indian Revenues
British Treasury
Consolidated Fund of Great Britain
Customs revenue of London port
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 8: Salaries and allowances of the Board of Control members and staff were charged directly to Indian revenues.

masteryZone.q: Question 9 (Section 2): True or False: The Charter Act of 1793 abolished the Maal Adalats (revenue courts), transferring their jurisdiction to the Diwani Adalats.
masteryZone.sol: Explanation 9: The Act consolidated the separation of revenue and judiciary, abolishing Maal Adalats.
